en: August (eighth month of the Gregorian and Julian calendars)
other, another — the masculine form (شخص ___ 'another person'); with different vowels, the last one, the end of something
moment, instant — chiefly في ___ واحد 'at one and the same time'; the base that the word for 'now' is built on
to add, to append, to annex; to cause to be followed by
chiefly in من ___ 'for the sake of, in order to'; an appointed term or deadline; and a bookish 'yes, indeed'

better, best — the comparative of 'good' (___ من 'better than'; من ال___ أن 'it is better to')
to go bankrupt, to become insolvent, to fail financially
to worry, to disturb, to trouble; to alarm, to unsettle
more, most; the greater part (___ من 'more than', ___ الناس 'most people') — the comparative of 'many, much'

to, that (before a verb); that (after say, think, know)
to slight, to disrespect, to insult, to abuse; to slur; to offend, to affront

to invent, to devise, to originate, to innovate

now, right now; at present, at the moment; up to now (حتى الآن)

who, which, that — the relative pronoun after a definite masculine singular noun (الرجل ___ جاء 'the man who came')

the dual ending on a noun or adjective, marking exactly two; also how 'that' and 'if' are written once the hamza is dropped

to show interest in, to be receptive; to reply to, to echo
to move, to be in motion; to set off, to depart
say..., I wonder... (precedes a yes-or-no question, sometimes follows يَا (yā))

to learn (something); also you know, do you know — 2nd sg. m. of عَلِمَ (ʕalima)
you are, she is; (after أن) to be — imperfect of كَانَ (kāna); also تَكَوَّنَ (takawwana) to be formed, to consist of (من)
that one, those — points at something feminine away from the speaker (___ المرأة 'that woman')
to be done, to be carried out — before a verbal noun it forms the passive (تم بناؤه “it was built”, تم فصلي “I was fired”); on its own to be completed, to be finished
instantaneousness, immediacy
a second, the unit of time (f.); as an adverb, again or for a second time; also second as an ordinal, feminine form
chandelier; the Pleiades

grandfather (جَدّ, m.; pl. أجداد); seriousness, earnestness (جِدّ) — بجدّ hard, in earnest (عمل بجد he worked hard), على محمل الجد seriously; also جِدّ 'very' before an adjective, though ordinary 'very' comes after the adjective and is spelled جدًّا, which is its own card
a surface where grain sheaves or dates are collected, a heap of harvest (Ḥijāzi and Yemenite form of جُرْن)
to make (someone do something), to cause; to put, to place, to set; (before a non-past verb) to begin to
general (a military officer)

condition, state, situation (m./f., pl. أحوال); حالًا right away, immediately; على أية حال / على كل حال anyway, in any case; في حال (أن) in case, in the event that; also the verb حَالَ to intervene, to prevent (دون)
love, affection (m.), as in الحب; also ʔaḥabba / yuḥibb, to love, to like; and ḥabb, grains, seeds, ḥabba, a grain, a pill

good, fine, handsome (adj. حَسَن, f. حسنة); also the Form II verb حسَّن to improve, to make better (حسّن معرفته he improved his knowledge); and the noun حُسْن goodness, beauty — حسن الحظ good luck
okay, all right, well then — said to accept what was said or to move on ('___, لنذهب' okay, let's go)
to happen, to occur, to take place; (with على) to get, to obtain, to receive
right, entitlement (m.; pl. حقوق) — يحق لـ to have the right to; truth, what is right (الحق معك you are right); حقًّا really, truly; also the verb حَقَّ to be true, to be due
campaign (f.), whether military, electoral or advertising; an attack, charge, offensive; also ḥamala, plural of حامل: bearers, holders
around, about, surrounding (___ العالم 'around the world'); on the subject of (كتاب ___ 'a book about')
outside, out of (___ البيت 'outside the house'); the outside, abroad (في ال___); going out
to go out, to leave, to exit (with مِن “out of”); to come out, to emerge; to go forth, to depart
to die out, to grow faint; to become low in volume or inaudible
inside, within (prep.); the inside, the interior (n., m.), as in في الداخل “indoors”; also the active participle of دخل, entering, incoming; and (rare) dāḵala, to befall, to come over
that, that one over there — the masculine form, pointing away from the speaker; the feminine counterpart is تلك
a tie, a thing with which one ties; a ribat (a frontier post where travellers and soldiers could stay)
to request, to ask politely, as in أرجوك “please” and يُرجى / الرجاء “kindly, please”; to hope for, to wish for
man (m.; pl. رِجال); also رِجْل leg, foot (f.; pl. أرجُل); rarely the verb رَجِلَ to go on foot
(with ما or لا) to still be, to still be doing — ما زال / لا يزال “he is still …”; on its own to go away, to disappear, to cease
Semitic; Sami (a male given name)

blackboard, whiteboard; slate
lady, madam, Mrs. — a woman addressed with respect; the feminine of 'master, sir'
concern, business — what someone has to do with a matter (هذا ___ي 'that's my business'); importance, standing
person, individual (m.; pl. أشخاص) — أي شخص anyone, شخص ما someone; also the verb شخَّص to diagnose, to identify
to feel, to sense (بـ something); to notice, to realize; also the nouns شَعْر hair (m.) and شِعْر poetry (m.)
shape, form, figure (m., pl. أشكال); kind, sort; بشكل — in a … way, as in بشكل عام “generally”; also šakkala, to form, to shape, to constitute
correct, right, true (___؟ 'really?'); sound, healthy, unbroken
nature, disposition, character (m., pl. طِباع); بالطبع / طبعًا — of course, naturally; also ṭabaʕa, to print, to stamp, to imprint, to type (طباعة printing, مطبعة press)
to ask for, to request; to order (food, goods); to demand, to require; to seek, to look for; also the noun ṭalab, request, application, order (m., pl. طلبات)
to know a person, place or thing, to be acquainted with; to recognise, to find out — knowing a fact is علم
dear, beloved — how a letter opens (___ي 'my dear'); precious, hard to come by; also mighty, held in honour
to know a fact, to learn of, to become aware that something is so; being acquainted with a person or place is عرف
on, on top of; against; must, have to (with a pronoun ending)

higher, highest, upper (feminine of أَعْلَى)
on you; you must, it is up to you (___ أن تذهب 'you have to go') — 'on' with the 2nd-person masculine ending

about, concerning; away from, off

to carry out, to do, to undertake — قام بـ + verbal noun is the ordinary way to say 'do' (قام بزيارة he paid a visit); to stand up, to rise, to get up
before, prior to (prep.) — قبل أن before (+ verb), من قبل before, previously; ago (قبل سنة a year ago); also the verb قَبِلَ to accept, to agree to

shirt (a sleeved upper-body garment)

but, however, yet — the bare form heading a contrast clause, with no 'and' prefix on the front

vat, wide-bellied bowl, trough

angels (plural of مَلْأَك / مَلَك)

self (f.; pl. أنفُس, نفوس) — the reflexive: نفسي myself, بنفسه by himself; the same (الوقت نفسه the same time); soul, psyche; also نَفَس breath (m.)
kind, type, sort (m., pl. أنواع); species, variety; as in أي نوع من “what kind of”; also nawwaʕa, to diversify, to vary

legs (f. plural of cama)

his, her, its — before a feminine noun (___ बहन — his sister)
his, her, its — before a masculine plural or oblique noun (___ बाद — after that; ___ साथ — with him)
him, her, it; to him, to her (also marks the one who needs or feels something)
one; a, an (a certain); single, sole
and; more, extra; other, different

do — the stem of करना, standing before रहा, सकना and the vector verbs (कर रहे हैं — are doing, कर सकते हो — you can do); also the conjunctive participle -कर, having done; and, as a literary noun, hand, arm (m.); tax (m.)
do, does — habitually, with a masculine singular subject (वह काम ___ है — he works)
do, does — habitually, with a masculine plural or respected subject (वे काम ___ हैं — they work)
doing, to do (infinitive before a postposition: करने के लिए — in order to do)
let's do, may do; please do — the polite request or suggestion form (हम क्या ___? — what should we do?)
will do — with a masculine plural or respected subject (हम कल ___ — we'll do it tomorrow)
do it! — the order or request you give a friend or peer (काम ___ — do the work)
said — masculine singular perfective of कहना (उसने कहा — he said; तुमने क्या कहा? — what did you say?); also a noun (m.): someone's word or bidding, as in कहा मानना — to do as one is told
of, 's — links owner to thing owned when that thing is masculine singular (राम ___ घर — Ram's house)
the Indian National Congress
the linking word that introduces what someone says or thinks (उसने कहा ___ ... — he said that ...)
did, made (past; under ने it agrees with a masculine singular object)
someone, anyone — the form used before a postposition (___ ने कहा — someone said; ___ को दो — give it to someone)
of, 's, belonging to (before a feminine noun); also did, made (past of करना)
of, 's, belonging to (before a masculine plural or oblique noun); also starts compound postpositions: के लिए — for, के साथ — with
only, merely — the formal, written counterpart of the everyday word for 'only' (___ एक बार — only once)
marks the one an action is aimed at — the definite object, or the receiver, 'to' (राम ___ बुलाओ — call Ram)
someone, anyone; a single unspecified one (___ आया है — someone has come; ___ बात नहीं — it's nothing)
what (___ हुआ? — what happened?); also turns a statement into a yes-or-no question, like a spoken question mark
eats, eat — masculine singular habitual participle of खाना, with हूँ/है (मैं चीज़ खाता हूँ — I eat cheese); also a noun: account, ledger (m.), as in a bank account (खाता खोलो — open an account)
went — masculine plural or respectful (वे चले ___ — they left); after a stem it completes the act: हो ___ — got done
went — masculine singular past (वह चला ___ — he went off); after a stem it completes the act: हो ___ — it happened
went off, left — masculine singular past (वह ___ गया — he went away); also, of a machine, ran or worked
let's go; come on, get moving — said to friends or peers (___, देर हो रही है — come on, it's getting late)
want — with a masculine singular subject (मैं जाना ___ हूँ — I want to go)
want — with a masculine plural or respected subject (वे जाना ___ हैं — they want to go)
is needed, is wanted (मुझे पानी ___ — I need water); with an infinitive, ought to (जाना ___ — should go)
leave, let go, drop — the bare stem (___ दो — let it go; ___ दिया — dropped it)
God; also a male given name, Jagdish
a need — the thing someone must have (मुझे पैसों की ___ है — I need money)
go — the bare stem standing before रहा and सकता (___ रहा है — is going); also 'go!' to a child or close friend
will go — masculine singular (वह कल ___ — he'll go tomorrow); also forms the future passive: किया ___ — will be done
go! — the order or request you give a friend or peer (घर ___ — go home)
goes — habitually, masculine singular (वह रोज़ ___ है — he goes daily); also forms the passive: किया ___ है — is done
know — with a masculine singular subject (मैं ___ हूँ — I know)
know — with a masculine plural or respected subject (आप ___ हैं — you know)
going, to go — the form before a postposition (___ के लिए — in order to go; ___ दो — let it be)
the one who or which — opens a clause describing something already named (___ आदमी आया — the man who came)
OK, all right — used to agree or say a thing is in order (___ है — that's OK); also exact (___ नौ बजे — at nine sharp)
you, at the तुम level — the form used when you did a completed action to an object (___ क्या कहा? — what did you say?)
your, at the तुम level — before a feminine noun (___ बहन — your sister)
your, at the तुम level — before a masculine plural or oblique noun (___ दोस्त — your friends)
you, to you (the तुम level — friends and peers)
then — the answering half of an if-clause (अगर ..., ___ ...); also a light emphasis, 'well', 'as for that'
was — with a masculine singular subject (वह वहाँ ___ — he was there); also makes a past tense: कर रहा ___ — was doing
was — with a feminine singular subject (वह घर पर ___ — she was at home)
were — with a masculine plural or respected subject (वे यहाँ ___ — they were here)
tooth (m.) — the anusvāra spelling of दाँत (गला हुआ दांत — the decayed tooth; दाँत साफ़ करना — to brush one's teeth); separately, a Sanskritic adjective: dental; restrained, subdued

gave — masculine singular perfective of देना (मैंने कुछ नहीं दिया — I gave nothing); as a completive vector after a stem it says the act was carried through: कर दिया — went and did it, छोड़ दिया — dropped it; also an oil lamp (m.), also spelled दीया

gave — feminine singular perfective of देना, agreeing with a feminine object under ने (उसने चेतावनी दी — he gave a warning); most often the completive vector taking that same agreement: नौकरी छोड़ दी — quit the job; also short for दीदी, elder sister (f.)
give — the stem of देना, standing before सकना, रहा and the vector verbs (नहीं दे सकता — I can't give, दे दो — give it here); also second/third-person singular present subjunctive: may give
look, see — the bare stem before रहा and सकता (___ रहा हूँ — I'm looking); also 'look!' to a child or close friend
saw, looked at — masculine singular past (मैंने उसे ___ — I saw him)
look!, see! — said to a friend or peer (इधर ___ — look here)
two (2); also give! — the तुम imperative of देना, and the same form as a completive vector: दे दो — hand it over, छोड़ दो — let it go, कर दो — just do it
no, not — the milder negative: in tag questions ('..., ___?' — isn't it?), in soft requests, and in 'neither ... nor'
new — feminine singular of नया, agreeing with a feminine noun (मेरी नई गाड़ी — my new car; कुछ नई बात? — anything new?)
goes after the doer when a completed past action has an object (राम ___ खाना खाया — Ram ate the food)
knowledge of a thing — ___ है means 'I know', ___ नहीं 'I don't know'; also a postal address
on, at (after a noun); but, however

got, obtained; was able to — masculine singular perfective of पाना, and after a bare stem the “managed to, could” construction (वह मदद नहीं कर पाया — he couldn't help; मैं उसे समझा पाया — I managed to make him understand); also a noun: the leg or foot of a piece of furniture (m.)
whole, complete, full — feminine of पूरा, agreeing with a feminine noun (पूरी रात — all night, पूरी तरह से — completely); also a puri (f.), the small deep-fried bread
again (___ से — once more); and then, after that (___ क्या हुआ? — then what happened?)
a telephone, or a call made on one — spelled plainly, without the nuqta dot (___ करना — to call someone)
enough, that's all — said to stop or finish something (___, और नहीं — that's enough, no more); just, simply
very — intensifying an adjective (___ अच्छा — very good); a lot of, many (___ लोग — many people)
used only in के ___ में — about, concerning (उसके ___ में — about him)
good, well — oblique/plural masculine of भला (तुम्हारे भले के लिये — for your own good; भले लोग — good people); and in भले (ही), the concessive: even if, even though, granted that
too, also — adds the item just named (मैं ___ आऊँगा — I'll come too); 'even' when it emphasizes
don't — the negative that goes in front of an order (___ जाओ — don't go; ___ करो — don't do it)

died; dead — masculine singular perfective of मरना (उसका बेटा कैसे मरा? — how did his son die?; मैं अभी तक मरा नहीं हूँ — I'm not dead yet; मरा हुआ — dead, deceased); also in मरा जा रहा हूँ — I'm dying of (hunger, thirst)

accept, agree, believe, obey — the stem of मानना, before लेना and जाना and in the imperative (मान लो — suppose, assume; हार मत मानो — don't give up; वह मान गया — he relented); also a noun: respect, honour; pride (m.), and in technical use a measure or value
hit, beat, kill — the bare stem (___ दिया — killed it; ___ डाला — finished it off); as a noun, a beating
meet; be found, be got — the bare stem (मुझे ___ गया — I found it; ___ जाएगा — it will be available)
got, was found; met — masculine singular past (मुझे पैसा ___ — I got the money; वह मुझे ___ — he met me)
me, to me; I, when needing or feeling something (मुझे भूख है — I am hungry)
my, mine — before a masculine singular noun (___ नाम — my name)
my, mine — before a feminine noun (___ बहन — my sister)
my, mine (before plural or oblique masculine nouns: मेरे दोस्त — my friends)
I — the form used when I did a completed action to an object (___ देखा — I saw it)
-ing (progressive: कर रहा है — is doing, masculine singular); stayed, remained
-ing, with a feminine subject (वह जा ___ है — she is going); also stayed, remained
-ing (progressive: कर रहे हैं — are doing, plural or respectful); stayed, remained
seem, feel; begin; be attached — the bare stem (___ रहा है — it seems; ___ गया — it took hold)
seems, feels — masculine singular (मुझे ___ है कि ... — it seems to me that ...); also is applied, is attached
for, for the sake of (in के लिए); also took, taken (past of लेना)
took — masculine singular past (मैंने पैसा ___ — I took the money); after a stem, did it for oneself (खरीद ___ — bought it)
take — the bare stem before सकना and the vector verbs (___ लो — take it; ___ जाओ — take it away)
people — the form used before a postposition (___ ने कहा — people said; ___ को बताओ — tell the people)
makes 'the one who or which ___' from a noun or an oblique infinitive (दूध ___ — the milkman; आने ___ — the one about to come)
in fact, actually — met almost only in ___ में (___ में हुआ क्या था? — what actually happened?)
changed, especially for the worse — damaged, impaired; mutilated, maimed
they, those; he, she (respectful, about one person)
that one; he, she, it — the everyday spoken spelling of the distal pronoun; also 'those'
can, is able to — after a bare verb stem, masculine singular subject (मैं कर ___ हूँ — I can do it)
can, be able to (after a bare stem; plural or respectful subject: कर सकते हैं)
everyone, everything; all of it — the plain everyday word (___ कुछ — everything; ___ लोग — all the people)
all of them without exception — the emphatic twin of सब, used with countable plural nouns and never for 'everything' (___ बच्चे आ गए — all the children have come)
in the company of, with — used as के ___ (मेरे ___ चलो — come with me); also company, companionship
only, just — nothing more than this, spelled plainly without the nuqta dot (___ दो रुपये — only two rupees)

learn — the stem of सीखना, standing before रहा, लेना and the vector verbs (वह क्या सीख रहा है? — what is he learning?; मैंने बजाना सीख लिया — I learned to play); also a noun: a lesson, a moral, a piece of advice (f.)
from (a place, person or time); by means of, with (a tool); than, in comparisons
a surname, Sen; also falcon

sleep — the stem of सोना, before जाना, रहा and in the imperative (सो जाओ — go to sleep; वह सो रहा है — he is sleeping); also the correlative pronoun answering जो: that one, so, therefore (जो हुआ सो हुआ — what is done is done)
we, us; I (colloquial)
our — before a masculine plural or oblique noun (___ घर में — in our house)
us, to us; we, when we need or must do something (___ जाना है — we have to go)
always, every single time (वह ___ देर से आता है — he is always late)
each, every — the ordinary spoken word standing before a singular noun, taken one at a time (___ दिन — every day; ___ कोई — everybody)
light (in weight) — masculine plural or oblique of हल्का (halkā)
yes; yeah, that's right (agreeing); yes? (answering when called)
attaches to a word to mean 'that one exactly, no other' (मैं ___ — me alone; आज ___ — this very day)
happened; became, turned out — masculine singular (क्या ___? — what happened?; वह खुश ___ — he became happy)
happened, became — masculine plural or respectful; after a participle, 'while ___ing' (जाते ___ — while going)
am (the form of होना used with मैं)
is; there is (used with a singular subject; a plural subject takes हैं)
are (the form used with तुम); be!; may be, might be (subjunctive)
will be; must be, probably is — masculine singular (वह घर पर ___ — he'll be at home)
is, happens, tends to be — masculine singular habitual participle of होना (ऐसा होता है — that is how it is; कुछ नहीं होता — nothing happens); also the counterfactual, होता तो — had it been so
being, happening — the form before a postposition (___ के बाद — after it happens; ___ वाला है — is about to happen)
event, function; program, show (television, radio); agenda (of a meeting)
introduces the purpose or wish behind an action, in formal or written style; speech says supaya
or (joining alternatives in statements and questions)
introduces a reported statement after verbs like say, know or hope ('I heard ___ he left')
to lend a hand with someone's task, to assist; tolong is the word used to ask the favour
to act, to take action; to behave in some way towards a matter (the ber- form of tindak, a step or an act)
and (joining words, phrases, and whole clauses)
marks where something is — in, at, on ('___ Jakarta'); before a person or a time, pada does this job
be lifted, be picked up; be appointed to a position; of a child, adopted (passive of angkat, to lift)
be arranged, be organised; be regulated or set by an authority, as prices are (passive of atur, to arrange)
be divided, be split up; be shared out among people; in sums, divided by (passive of bagi, to share out)
be helped, be assisted, be given a hand with a task (passive of bantu, to help)
be carried, be brought along; be taken somewhere, as a patient to hospital (passive of bawa, to carry)
be formed, be shaped; be set up, of a committee or a government (passive di- form of membentuk, to form)
be killed, be murdered, be put to death (passive of bunuh, to kill)
be printed, be run off; in sport, of a goal or points, be scored (passive of cetak, printing)
be suspected, be alleged; be guessed at - and before a verb, allegedly (passive of duga, to suppose)
be supported, be backed - of a plan, a candidate, a claim (passive of dukung, to support)
be destroyed, be demolished, be smashed up (passive of hancur, shattered)
be produced, be generated; come out as the result of a process (passive of hasil, a result)
be sold, be sold off; be up for sale, be on offer (passive of menjual, to sell)
be defeated, be beaten - of a team or an opponent (passive of kalah, to lose)
be taken out, be put out; be issued; be thrown out or dropped, as from a team (passive of keluar, to go out)
be sent, be sent off - of a letter, a parcel, a message (passive of mengirim, to send)
be seen, be looked at; seen from somewhere, as a viewpoint on a thing (passive of lihat, to see)
be played - a game, a piece of music, a part on stage (passive of main, to play)
be put to use, be made use of; be taken advantage of, be exploited (passive of manfaat, benefit)
be asked to do something, be requested; of a thing, be asked for (passive of minta, to ask for)
be given a name, be named after a person or a place (passive of nama, a name)
be called, be given a name - as in our galaxy is called the Milky Way (passive of nama, a name)
be declared, be officially stated - found guilty, ruled valid, tested positive (passive of menyatakan, to declare)
be operated, be run, be worked - of a machine, a line or a service (passive of operasi, operation)
be looked at, be gazed at; be regarded or seen as something (passive of pandang, to look at)
be called, be summoned, be sent for - of a person called by name (passive of panggil, to call)
be put up, be installed, be fitted - a sign, a lamp, a device (passive of pasang, to set in place)
be influenced, be affected by something, be shaped by it (passive of pengaruh, influence)
be trusted, be believed; trustworthy, reliable, worth taking at his word (passive of percaya, to trust)
be chosen, be picked out; be elected to a post (passive of pilih, to choose)
be designed, be drawn up, be planned out in advance (passive of rancang, to design)
be planned, be arranged in advance - by design rather than by accident (passive of rencana, a plan)
be provided, be laid on, be made ready for someone (passive of menyediakan, to provide)
plus, in adding numbers, as in three plus two; more generally, be added to, be topped up (passive of menambah, to add)
be added - an entry put onto a list, an ingredient put into a dish (passive of tambah, to add)
be received, be accepted; be taken in, be made welcome, as of a guest in a house (passive of menerima, to receive)
be translated into another language (passive of terjemah, translation)
be rejected, be turned down, be refused - an offer, an application (passive of menolak, to reject)
be aimed at, be directed to, be addressed to a person (passive of tuju, to aim)
be closed, be shut; be shut down for good, of a factory or a road (passive of tutup, to close)
to wish for, to long for — a felt desire, and the more formal word; mau is the plain everyday 'want'
if, in the event that (formal and written; everyday speech says kalau)
if; when, whenever; as for, speaking of (everyday; jika is the formal word)
you (singular, informal, for friends and peers; Anda is the polite form)
asks at what time something happens ('___ do you arrive?')
a word — the unit speech and vocabulary are counted in; also introduces a quoted speaker ('___ Budi, ...' = Budi says)
you, one person — the clipped, blunt form of songs, poetry and very close talk; kamu is the everyday informal
to go back to where one was; also the polite reply to a thank-you — pulang is going home specifically
asks for the reason ('___ are you late?'); the everyday spoken form, where mengapa is the formal one
at the moment that — joins a clause saying when the other happened ('___ I arrived, it was raining')
marks a comparison — more, -er ('this one is ___ expensive than that')
and so — heads the consequence clause, mostly formal or written ('if it rains, ___ we stay in')
asks which one out of several ('the red or the blue — ___?'); also the question root after di, ke and dari
each on their own part, respectively ('we paid for ourselves')
but rather, but instead - it follows bukan and puts the true thing in place of the one just denied, as in not a doctor but a teacher
to understand, to grasp; to have a real command of a language or a subject (the meN-...-i form of paham, understanding)
to play something - a game, a piece of music, a part in a story (the meN-...-kan form of main, to play)
to eat up, to devour; to take up time, money or effort (the meN- form of makan, to eat)
to make use of, to take advantage of - a chance, a situation, a resource (the meN-...-kan form of manfaat, benefit)
to call someone, to call out to them; to summon or send for a person (the meN- form of panggil, to call)
to discuss, to go over, to deal with a subject (the meN- form of bahas)
to tell apart, to distinguish one thing from another (the meN-...-kan form of beda, a difference)
to tell someone, to let them know, to inform them of something (beri, to give, plus tahu, to know)
to meet or fulfil a need, a demand or a condition; to fill a space right up (the meN-...-i form of penuh, full)
to rule, to govern, to hold power over a country (the meN- form of perintah, a command)
to introduce - one person to another, or a subject to an audience (the memper-...-kan form of kenal, to be acquainted)
to produce, to manufacture, to turn out goods (the meN- form of produksi, production)
to handle, to deal with, to take charge of a matter (the meN-...-i form of tangan, a hand)
to cover, to include, to take in - of a scope, a rule or a range (the meN- form of cakup)
to note down, to write down, to record; to register a figure or a result (the meN- form of catat, a note)
to score - a goal, a run, points in a game; also to print, to run off copies (the meN- form of cetak, printing)
to oppose, to go against, to stand up against a person or an idea (the meN- form of tentang; the bare root is the preposition about)
to hold, to put on - a party, a meeting, an event; to bring something into being (the meN-...-kan form of ada, to exist)
to invite someone along, to ask them to come and do something with you (the meN- form of ajak)
to defeat, to beat an opponent; to overcome something (the meN-...-kan form of kalah, to lose)
to contain, to have something in it, of a dish or a drink; of a woman, to be pregnant (the meN- form of kandung)
asks for the reason, in formal or written style; ordinary speech uses kenapa instead
to arrange, to organise; to regulate or set - traffic, files, a machine (the meN- form of atur)
to take out, to bring out; to issue or give off; to lay out money on something (the meN-...-kan form of keluar, to go out)
to know a person, to be acquainted with them; to recognise something (the meN- form of kenal, acquainted)
to catch the meaning of what someone says ('I don't ___ the question'); paham is the firmer grasp
to stop something, to bring it to a halt, to put an end to it (the meN-...-kan form of henti, a halt)
to run something - a machine, a program, a business; to carry a plan out (the meN-...-kan form of jalan, to go)
to wait, to wait for a person or a thing to come (the meN- form of tunggu, to wait)
to spread, to get about, to reach far and wide - of news, a language, a disease (the meN- form of sebar, to scatter)
to finish, to get done; to settle or solve a problem (the meN-...-kan form of selesai, finished)
even though — concedes a fact the main clause overrides; the me- form carrying -pun, twin of walaupun
at, on — used before a time or a person ('___ Monday', 'it depends ___ him'), where di marks a place
to have a firm grasp of a subject; also the understanding itself; mengerti is catching a meaning
bound to be so, certain — the speaker's confidence that a fact holds ('he's ___ home by now')
general election - the nationwide vote for president and the legislature, held every five years
the country at the western edge of the Iberian peninsula, west of Spain, with Lisbon as its capital
guided missile - a rocket that steers itself to its target
follows what it limits — just, only ('two ___' = only two); also 'go ahead and' in an invitation
I, me — the polite, neutral word for oneself, safe with strangers; aku is the intimate one
in the role or capacity of ('she works ___ a nurse')
a, one - the counter placed before an animal, as in a cat or a dog, where English says just a (se-, one, plus ekor, tail)
with the result that — links an outcome to its cause within one sentence ('it rained so hard ___ we stayed in'); jadi is the spoken 'so'
follows an adjective to intensify it ('good ___' = very good); also one time, on one occasion
all (before the noun); everyone, everything (standing on its own)
a, one - placed before a noun naming a person, as in a doctor or a child (built on orang, the classifier Indonesian uses for people)
every one in a set, no member left out; the longer, se- prefixed form, standing before the noun ('___ day')
introduces the purpose of an action ('come early ___ we can talk'); the everyday word, agar the formal one
but; however (everyday form of the more formal tetapi)
of course, naturally — granting what the hearer already assumes, often followed by saja
to catch fire; burnt, on fire (ter- form of bakar 'to burn' — happens to the subject)
involved, mixed up in something; caught up in an affair (the ter- form of libat, so the state rather than the act)
television - both the set in the room and broadcasting itself, in the short two-letter form that is commoner in Dutch than the full word (de; plural adds -'s)
for, intended for; in order to, so as to (before a verb)
even though — concedes a fact the main clause overrides; the wa- form carrying -pun, twin of meskipun
yes; right?, isn't it? (tag at the end of a sentence); okay? (softening a request)
links a noun to the clause describing it ('the book ___ I read'); also picks out 'the one that'
to (indirect object); at, in (a place or time); to (before an infinitive)
we have ('___ due figli'); the auxiliary for our past ('___ visto' 'we saw')

could, was able to — the past singular of the ability verb ('ik ___ niet komen').
buy: I buy; buy! (present and imperative of kopen); as a noun, a purchase, a deal; te koop — for sale
costs: it costs; he/she/it costs (present of kosten) — hoeveel kost het? how much does it cost?; also a noun, de kost — board, keep, livelihood, as in de kost verdienen, to earn a living
to cost; to take, require (time, effort); also the plural of kost — costs, expenses
powers, forces; strengths (plural of kracht)
got, received — I/you/he/she/it got (singular past of krijgen)
I get, I receive (ik krijg wat ik wil); get! (imperative of krijgen); (archaic) war
you can, you are able to — second-person singular present of kunnen; the fuller form kunt is equally standard, and u kunt is the polite one
can: you can, in 'jij ___' and 'u ___' — present of the ability verb.
to kiss (ik zou je graag kussen — I'd like to kiss you); as a noun, het kussen — pillow, cushion (ik ben geen kussen!, I'm not a pillow); also kisses, the plural of kus
de kust — coast, shoreline, seaside (drie kilometer naar de kust; we gaan naar de kust); also you kiss, he/she kisses (present of kussen — ik wil dat je me kust)
came — I/you/he/she/it came (singular past of komen)
late (not early); also let, leave: I let; let…! (present and imperative of laten — laat maar, laat zien)
last, most recent (superlative of laat): voor het laatst — for the last time; as an adverb, recently, the other day — laatst dacht ik aan je, the other day I thought of you
laugh: I laugh; laugh! — present and imperative of lachen (lach me niet uit, don't laugh at me; wat lach je nou?, what are you laughing at?); as a noun, de lach — a laugh, a smile
lay, was lying down — I/you/he/she/it lay (singular past of liggen); also was located, sat or stood somewhere
longer; taller — comparative of lang, long or tall; with niet or geen it means no longer, not any more
read: I/he/she read — past singular of lezen (gisteren las ik een interessant verhaal, yesterday I read an interesting story); also I weld (present of lassen), and a noun, de las — a weld, a joint
to let, to allow; to have something done (ik laat het zien — I'll show it); laten we… — let's…; to leave (as it is)
later, afterwards (comparative of laat — ik bel je later terug; drie uur later); when I'm grown up (als ik later groot ben); as an adjective: later, subsequent

seemed, looked (like): I/he/she/it seemed (singular past of lijken — ze leek niet blij, she did not seem happy; het leek erop dat, it seemed that; leek hij op een dokter?, did he look like a doctor?); also a noun, layman, non-expert
learn, teach: I learn; learn! (present and imperative of leren): Leer deze namen uit het hoofd — learn these names by heart; also a noun, leather (het leer), and doctrine, teachings (de leer)
put, lay: I put, I lay; put!, lay! (present and imperative of leggen — leg dat boek neer, put that book down; leg het uit, explain it); also a noun, the laying of eggs
to be alive, to have life ('lang ___!'); as a noun, life — 'to reside somewhere' is wonen.
lives: the life each person or creature has (plural of leven)
darling, sweetheart, baby — an affectionate name for a partner (het; diminutive of lief, sweet, lovely)
walked; ran — I/you/he/she/it walked (singular past of lopen)
let, allowed — I/you/he/she/it let (singular past of laten); with zien it means showed, and it also covers having something done
rather, sooner — I would rather, I prefer to (comparative of lief, dear, sweet); the everyday way to say you would prefer something
soft drink, fizzy drink, soda (carbonated sweet drink based on processed fruit juice)
lied: I/he/she lied — past singular of liegen (hij loog tegen ons, he lied to us; je loog tegen me!, you lied to me!); also a noun: lye, caustic solution

walk, run: I walk; walk! (present and imperative of lopen — loop niet zo snel, don't walk so fast; loop jij naar school?); also a noun, course, duration (in de loop van de dag — in the course of the day), and the barrel of a gun
the clipped spoken form of 'him, it' as an object ('ik zie ___'), written with an apostrophe in careful Dutch.
months (plural of de maand)
but, however — turns a sentence against the one before it ('klein ___ sterk'); also a softening particle ('doe het ___').
buddy, mate, pal — het maatje (Tom is mijn maatje, Tom is my buddy); a size, a notch (een maatje groter, a size bigger); also maatjesharing, young salted herring
may, is allowed to — the singular present of the permission verb ('___ ik iets vragen?').
easier, simpler (comparative of makkelijk)

ways, methods (plural of de manier — op verschillende manieren, in different ways); manners, good behaviour (waar zijn je manieren?)
men (plural of de man)

been through, experienced, lived through (past participle of meemaken)

the stressed object form of 'I', used after a preposition or for contrast ('aan ___', 'niet hem maar ___'); me when unstressed.

fog, mist (de mist); also he/she/it misses, is missing (present of missen): Tom mist een tand — Tom is missing a tooth
was allowed to, could — I/you/he/she/it was allowed to (singular past of mogen); at the head of a clause it also means should it happen that, if by any chance
mothers, mums (plural of moeder)
had to, needed to — I/you/he/she/it had to (singular past of moeten)
must, have to; need to (I/you/he must — present of moeten)
to have to, to be obliged to — the verb behind 'must' ('we ___ nu gaan').
a moment, just a second (het; diminutive of moment)
murders (plural of moord); also a verb, to kill, to murder — the everyday transitive verb is vermoorden
a surname, Mulder, originating as an occupation, equivalent to English Miller
after, once something is over ('___ het eten gaan we weg').

took — I/you/he/she/it took (singular past of nemen)

shot down, gunned down: shot and felled (past participle of neerschieten)
just now, a moment ago ('hij is ___ weg'); also neat and tidy; and the mesh you catch fish with.

nothing, not a thing — the neutral form ('ik zie ___'); niks is its casual spoken twin.
nothing — the casual, spoken form ('het is ___'); niets is the neutral, written one.
well… — the filler that opens or softens a reply ('___, misschien'); also an impatient 'come on!'.

fired, dismissed, let go from a job; also discharged or released (past participle of ontslaan)
kidnapped, abducted (past participle of ontvoeren)
our — the possessive used before a de-word ('___ buurman'); ons before a het-word.
on, on top of; at, in (op school, op kantoor); up; finished, all gone
solved, worked out; dissolved (past participle of oplossen)
picked up, answered, as in a phone; with contact, got in touch; also recorded, or admitted to hospital (past participle of opnemen)
locked in, shut up, imprisoned (past participle of opsluiten)
ears; also the handles on a cup or mug (plural of oor)
older (comparative of oud): drie jaar ouder dan ik — three years older than me; ouder worden — to grow older; also a noun, a parent (usually plural, ouders)
parents, a mother and father together (plural of de ouder, a parent)
about, on the topic of ('een film ___ Rome'); across or above; and 'left, remaining'.
convinced, persuaded; certain of something (past participle of overtuigen)
horses (plural of paard)
pack, package; suit (set of clothes); also grab!, take! (imperative of pakken — pak je spullen, pak 'm)
Paris (the capital and largest city of France)
fitted, suited: I/he/she/it fitted (singular past of passen)
the people a doctor treats; those under medical care (plural of patiënt)

pills, tablets (plural of pil)
places, spots, seats (plural of plaats); also a verb, to place, to put; to qualify (in sports)
Poland (a country in Central Europe)
wallet, billfold; also portfolio (a post, a set of responsibilities)
talk, speak — the present tense of praten (je praat te veel; praat niet zo tegen hem); as a noun: talk, chatter
problems, troubles (plural of het probleem)
points, marks or scores; dots and full stops; the sharp tips of things (plural of punt)

advice, counsel (de raad): hij vroeg om mijn raad — he asked for my advice; also a council, board (gemeenteraad — town council); and I advise; guess! (present and imperative of raden) — raad eens, guess what
I hit, I touch; hit!, touch! (present and imperative of raken): raak dit niet aan — don't touch this; also an adjective, on target, well-aimed — een rake opmerking, a telling remark
strange, weird, odd (inflected form of raar): een rare vraag — a strange question; rare streken — funny business; as a noun, de rare — the odd one, the weirdo

a right, entitlement (het recht om te zwijgen — the right to remain silent; recht hebben op, to be entitled to); law, justice; also straight, upright (zit recht — sit up straight; recht vooruit, straight ahead)
reasons, grounds for doing something (plural of reden)
rode, drove: I/you/he/she/it rode or drove (singular past of rijden)
to arrange, to sort out, to see to: dat zal ik voor je regelen — I'll arrange that for you; also to regulate, to control
lines of writing; rules (plural of de regel) — the lines you read between, and the rules of a school or a game

seconds, the units of time (plural of de seconde)

tracks, traces; railway tracks (plural of spoor): Steek de sporen niet over — don't cross the tracks; also a verb, to spur; to travel by train; to be consistent, to add up

things, belongings, stuff (plural of het spul) — what you pack and carry; the plural is the everyday form

to step, to walk (te moe om verder te stappen, too tired to walk any further); to go out on the town (we gaan stappen); also steps (plural of de stap — de eerste stappen); to march

to sting, prick, stab (een wesp steekt, a wasp stings); to put, stick, insert (dingen in een doos steken, to put things in a box); oversteken — to cross (de straat oversteken); as a noun, stitches, stabs (plural of de steek)
to ask, to pose: een vraag stellen — to ask a question; to state, to put forward (wij stellen dat, we hold that); to position, to place; also plural of stel — couples, sets
put, set, pose: you/he/she/it puts (present of stellen); also a noun, stilt
stronger (comparative of sterk)
stars: the bodies in the night sky, and famous people (plural of ster)
a surname originating as a patronymic
died — I/you/he/she/it died (singular past of sterven)
stop!, quit! (imperative of stoppen, usually stop met … — stop met praten); I stop; as a noun: a plug, a stopper; a fuse
a little piece, a bit; also a short article or item (het; diminutive of stuk)
pieces, parts, bits; also documents or papers, and as an adverb, by far (plural of stuk)
to send (het boek naar mij te sturen — to send me the book; kun je dat per e-mail sturen?); also to steer, to drive, to guide

send: I send; send! (present and imperative of sturen — stuur mij een foto, send me a photo; stuur versterking, send reinforcements); also I steer, I drive; as a noun, het stuur — steering wheel, handlebars
the clipped spoken form of the neuter 'the, it' ('___ is koud'), written with an apostrophe in careful Dutch.
teeth (plural of tand)
to (with an infinitive, often after om); too, excessively
a phone call (het; diminutive of telefoon)
times, ages: long stretches, as in not seen you for ages; also grammatical tenses (plural of tijd)
a little while, a short time (het; diminutive of tijd)
all the same, even so — goes against what was expected ('het regende, ___ gingen we'); also the tag 'right?' in a question.
to, towards — the form tot takes in ertoe, waartoe and in separable verbs (toegeven, toedoen); aan iets toe zijn — to be ready for, due for; shut, closed (de deur is toe); toe maar! — go on!
show!, show me — imperative of tonen (toon me je papieren!, show me your papers); I show; as a noun, de toon — tone, note (op een boze toon; de toon zetten)

appetite, hunger (ik heb geen trek — I'm not hungry; trek hebben in, to fancy); also I pull; pull! (present and imperative of trekken — trek de stekker eruit, unplug it); a migration, a trek; a feature, a trait
pulled, drew: I/he/she pulled — past singular of trekken (ze trok de deur open, she pulled the door open); wegtrekken — to drain away, to fade (alle kleur trok weg uit zijn gezicht)
television - both the set in the room and broadcasting itself, in the short two-letter form that is commoner in Dutch than the full word (de; plural adds -'s)
invited, asked to come (past participle of uitnodigen)
hours: sixty-minute stretches of time (plural of uur)
your — the polite possessive, the one that goes with u ('___ naam, alstublieft'); jouw is the informal one.
fathers, dads; also of a father, the possessive, as in my father's mother (plural or possessive of vader)

fall: I fall; fall! (present and imperative of vallen — val dood, drop dead; val aan, attack; val me niet lastig, don't bother me); as a noun, a trap, a snare (het is een val — it's a trap), and a fall
of (possession); from (origin, starting point); by (a creator)
stuck, fixed in place ('de deur zit ___'); also 'surely, I bet' before a guess ('dat is ___ leuk').
changed — have or has changed (past participle of veranderen)
connected, joined, linked; also bandaged (past participle of verbinden)
further, farther; further on, any more — comparative of ver, far; with niets or niemand it means else, as in nothing else, nobody else
earned, made, as in money; also deserved (past participle of verdienen)
disappeared, vanished: I/you/he/she/it disappeared (singular past of verdwijnen)
stories, tales (plural of verhaal); also a verb, to recount, and to recover (costs) from someone
sold: has sold (past participle), and I/you/he/she/it sold (singular past of verkopen)
I sell — present of verkopen (ik verkoop bloemen, I sell flowers; ik verkoop mijn auto met verlies); as a noun, de verkoop — sale, sales (de verkoop van het huis)
lost, mislaid; was beaten: I/you/he/she/it lost (singular past of verliezen)
told — have or has told (past participle of vertellen)
leave, depart: I leave; leave! (present and imperative of vertrekken): Ik vertrek morgen — I leave tomorrow; also a noun, departure, and a room, quarters
left, departed, set off: I/you/he/she/it left (singular past of vertrekken)
fell — I/you/he/she/it fell (singular past of vallen)
enemies, foes (plural of vijand)

fingerprints (plural of vingerafdruk)

formerly, in the past, in the old days — used to (vroeger was alles beter, everything used to be better; Tom was vroeger een slaaf, Tom used to be a slave; net als vroeger, just like before); also earlier (comparative of vroeg) and former, of former times (in vroeger dagen, in days gone by)
women; wives (plural of de vrouw)
where, in which place (waar is hij?); true (dat is niet waar — that's not true); where, the place that

weeks (plural of week — drie weken geleden, three weeks ago; de deadline is over drie weken, the deadline is three weeks from now); rarely a verb, to soak, to soften
the opposite of not (indeed; I do; it is so); also no less than, as much as (expressing amazement)

bags, pockets, sacks (plural of zak): Maak je zakken leeg — empty your pockets; also a verb, to sink, to drop, to lower, and to fail (an exam)
will, shall — the singular helper that puts a verb in the future ('ik ___ het morgen doen').
sat, was sitting (past singular of zitten — ze zat naast me, she sat next to me; ik zat vast, I was stuck); fed up with, sick of (iets zat zijn); drunk (informal)
she; they; them (everyday unstressed form; zij/hen when stressed)
say: I say ('ik ___ niets'); also the command 'say!' and the attention-getter 'hey…'.
said — the past singular of 'to say' ('hij ___ niets tegen mij').
himself, herself, themselves — the plain reflexive object after a third-person subject ('hij wast ___'); zichzelf is the emphatic twin.
